misconceptions.description: Treating the first TeachGen@i output as usable without checking it against grade level, equity, or accuracy before it reaches students
misconceptions.trigger: transcript shows a prompt and an output accepted as-is with no teacher edit
misconceptions.feedback: Troubleshoot the output. Check reading level, biased examples, and accuracy before any item reaches a student.

misconceptions.description: Submitting a clean final prompt with no record of any suggestion the teacher modified or rejected, hiding where teacher judgment intervened
misconceptions.trigger: transcript shows only the polished final prompt and no edit history
misconceptions.feedback: Keep at least one rejected or modified suggestion in the transcript so your judgment is inspectable.

misconceptions.description: Letting TeachGen@i auto-grade open-response work or auto-contact families, handing over judgment and consent decisions that belong to the teacher and district policy
misconceptions.trigger: teacher accepts a tool offer to grade short answers or email parents automatically
misconceptions.feedback: Short-answer judgment and family contact are teacher and policy decisions. Reject tool defaults that cross that boundary.

misconceptions.description: Not noticing that generated items assume student background (family trips, household income) and so disadvantage some students
misconceptions.trigger: transcript leaves a context-loaded example unedited
misconceptions.feedback: Scan generated examples for assumptions about income or experience and swap them for context-neutral ones.
